teaser: All 53 sgit.ai site repositories counted: 45 live sites, 1,679 commits, 5,419 pages, growth in bursts and a long tail.
core_idea: Counted on 21 October 2026, the sgit.ai estate is 53 website repositories and 45 live sites that grew in bursts of about ten sites a week; most sites are built in a session or two, four repositories hold most of the work, and families of hub and instance sites are appearing, which is why naming needs a rule.

nodes.label: Growth in bursts
nodes.summary: About ten new sites in each of five weeks.

nodes.label: A long tail
nodes.summary: Four repositories hold 62% of commits; median seven.

nodes.label: A site is cheap

nodes.label: Families of sites
nodes.summary: Hubs with instances; API sites; editions.

nodes.label: Loose ends
nodes.summary: One not serving, four without sitemaps, four hosts to rename.

quotes.text: Four repositories, sgit.ai, the newsroom, graphs and PKI, hold 62% of all the commits.
A site that renders a book or a corpus can be large and young at the same time.
That is not a sign of neglect.

figures.caption: Fifty-three repositories in eleven weeks. Left: new site repositories each week, with the running total underneath. Right: commits across all of them each week, peaking at 331 in the week of 12 October.
Commits per repository, the fourteen busiest. sgit.ai has 495, the newsroom 262, graphs 139 and PKI 137; together they hold 62% of the 1,679 commits.
Pages listed in each live site's sitemap, the fourteen largest. The newsroom lists 1,282 and its Portuguese edition 929; sgit.ai 604 and the Gen Z Developers book 496.

The families held against the convention agreed on 21 October: plural for the hub, singular for the instance. The twins and hooks families follow it; four provider and game hosts break it; the demo, hook and twin instances are reserved, with no site yet.
